formHandling.title: Form handling
formHandling.summary: React Hook Form with Zod schema factories, reusable controlled fields and server-side errors mapped back onto the inputs.
highlights: Schema factories receive t(), so validation messages follow the active language.
Fields such as InputField wrap useController, so screens never use Controller directly.
One useFormField hook wires the label id, aria-invalid and aria-describedby.
Validates on the first submit, then on change, so typing is never interrupted.
Mutation hooks invalidate the list query on success.
API field errors are mapped back onto the inputs with applyServerFieldErrors.

projectStructure.title: Project structure & architecture rules
projectStructure.summary: A layered, feature-based structure whose import rules are enforced by ESLint, not left to convention.
highlights: Five layers: router → modules → shared → core → _widgets. Imports only flow downwards.
eslint-plugin-boundaries fails the build when a layer imports upwards.
A custom ESLint rule keeps folders equal to the React render tree.
Role suffixes such as -section, -card and -dialog are enforced by lint.
No barrel files, no API folders inside modules, specs live under src/test.
Form fields wrap React Hook Form's useController, imported through @ui/form.
CI runs format, contract check, typecheck, lint, tests, build and bundle budget.

dataLayer.title: Data layer: API → service → query → converter
dataLayer.summary: A one-way data flow where each step has a single job: typed HTTP call, business mapping, cache keys and view model.
highlights: core/apis holds one typed Axios call per endpoint, nothing else.
Services unwrap responses and map UI parameters to the wire format.
queryOptions factories own the cache keys; a mutation invalidates one root key.
Converters run in select: the cache keeps the DTO, screens derive view models.
The abort signal reaches Axios, so leaving a screen cancels its requests.

globalTypes.title: Global utility types
globalTypes.summary: One ambient globals.type.d.ts declares the helper types every file uses, with no imports needed.
highlights: tsconfig includes globals.type.d.ts, so its types are available everywhere without an import.
The file has no imports or exports, which keeps it a global script.
Nullable<T> for fields the API sends as null, such as avatarUrl.
Maybe<T> for optional values, Nillable<T> when null and undefined are both possible.
ID accepts string or number keys, so the same DTO fits any backend.
ValueOption is the one option shape for select, combobox, radio and multi-select.

routing.title: Routing, lazy pages & prefetch loaders
routing.summary: A data router with one route file per module, lazy-loaded pages and loaders that prefetch the first query in parallel with the page code.
highlights: Every page is a lazy named export, so each module ships as its own chunk.
Loaders check access, then prefetch with the exact query options the page uses.
Loaders never block navigation or throw; the page query owns loading and errors.
Breadcrumbs are declared on the route with typed translation keys.

designSystem.title: Design system on shadcn/ui + CVA
designSystem.summary: Primitives ported from shadcn/ui into the project, one part per file, styled only with design tokens and typed variants.
highlights: CVA variants are typed and exposed as constants, never passed as raw strings.
Classes use only design tokens (bg-primary, h-button), never raw colors or sizes.
React 19 style: ref is a prop, no forwardRef, the React Compiler memoizes.
Radix accessibility is kept: focus rings, aria attributes and screen-reader labels.

designTokens.title: Design tokens & theming in CSS
designTokens.summary: Every color, size and shadow is a named token defined once in CSS. Components use the token name, so a rebrand or dark mode is a change of values, not of components.
highlights: Components never use raw values such as #5a7d36 or bg-green-700. They use a role: bg-primary, text-muted-foreground, border-error-border.
Each token has one value in :root and one in .dark. Dark mode only swaps the values, so components need no dark: classes.
@theme inline turns each CSS variable into Tailwind classes (bg-*, text-*, border-*), with autocompletion and opacity modifiers such as bg-primary/90.
Status colors come in sets of three (background, text, border), so every badge and alert looks the same.
Sizes from the design are tokens too: h-input, h-button, rounded-card, shadow-card. The radius scale is derived from a single --radius.
Base styles and custom utilities (scrollbar-thin) live in the same file, so the whole visual language is in one place.
steps: Token values for light and dark
